games.title: Rebelstar Raiders
games.note: Julian Gollop's first turn-based squad tactics game, made for the ZX Spectrum.

games.title: Laser Squad
games.note: The Gollop brothers' squad tactics game; work on a sequel turned into UFO: Enemy Unknown.

games.title: XCOM 2
games.note: Set twenty years after the aliens won; XCOM is now a resistance movement on a mobile base.

games.title: Phoenix Point
games.note: Julian Gollop's return to squad tactics, made in Sofia: free aiming at body parts and mutating alien enemies.

games.title: Jagged Alliance
games.note: Hire mercenaries with distinct personalities to free an island, fighting in turn-based battles.

games.title: Jagged Alliance 2
games.note: Mercenaries bicker, quit and remember how you treated them while you retake a country sector by sector.

games.title: Famicom Wars
games.note: Intelligent Systems' turn-based console wargame; the same team then made Fire Emblem.

games.title: Advance Wars
games.note: The first Wars game released outside Japan, with commanders whose special powers can turn a battle.

games.title: First Queen
games.note: A Japanese PC-98 strategy RPG with crowded real-time battles; Fire Emblem's creator cited it as an influence.

games.title: Silver Ghost
games.note: A Japanese PC-88 real-time tactics game that Shining Force creator Hiroyuki Takahashi cited as inspiration.

games.title: Shining Force
games.note: Hiroyuki Takahashi's tactics RPG for Sega, with a big cast of recruitable fighters.

games.title: Langrisser
games.note: Released in the West as Warsong; commanders lead squads of hired troops.

games.title: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together
games.note: Yasumi Matsuno's war story of ethnic conflict, with choices that split the plot.

games.title: Final Fantasy Tactics
games.note: Directed by Yasumi Matsuno after he joined Square from Quest, maker of Tactics Ogre.

games.title: Front Mission
games.note: Turn-based battles between customizable mechs called wanzers.

games.title: Disgaea
games.note: Level caps in the thousands, throwable allies and geo panels that change the battlefield.

games.title: Sakura Wars
games.note: Mixes dating-sim story scenes with turn-based steam-powered mech battles in 1920s Tokyo.

games.title: Valkyria Chronicles
games.note: Its BLiTZ system mixes turn-based command with steering each soldier yourself in real time, under fire.

games.title: Into the Breach
games.note: Every enemy attack is shown before it lands, so each turn is a puzzle of shoving monsters into harm's way.

games.title: Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle
games.note: Nintendo let Ubisoft's Milan studio put Mario and the Rabbids in a turn-based tactics game.

games.title: Wargroove
games.note: Pixel-art turn-based tactics with commanders who fight on the field, plus a full map and campaign editor.

games.title: Cannon Fodder
games.note: Each fallen recruit gets a gravestone on Boot Hill, set to the jaunty theme 'War Has Never Been So Much Fun'.

games.title: Artillery Duel
games.note: First released on the Bally Astrocade in 1982: two cannons trade shots over hills, adjusting angle and power.

games.title: Scorched Earth
games.note: Wendell Hicken's shareware hit, subtitled 'The Mother of All Games', with dozens of weapons to buy between rounds.

games.title: Gorillas
games.note: A sample program shipped with QBasic in MS-DOS 5.0: two gorillas on skyscrapers throw exploding bananas.

games.title: GunBound
games.note: A free-to-play online artillery game from Korea, fought with cartoon vehicles called mobiles.

games.title: Worms
games.note: Andy Davidson began it in 1990 on a Casio graphing calculator under the name Artillery.

links.took: Julian Gollop's turn-based squad combat with action points and line of sight.
links.added: A computer opponent, equipment to buy and destructible scenery.
links.extra: Same designer.

links.took: The squad combat engine: time units, line of sight and destructible terrain.
links.added: A global strategy layer of bases, research, funding nations and alien autopsies.
links.extra: Mythos began UFO as a Laser Squad sequel.

links.took: The whole X-COM formula of base building, research and squad battles.
links.added: An undersea setting, tougher aliens and multi-stage missions.

src.t: Wikipedia: X-COM: Terror from the Deep

links.took: Two-action turns, cover and soldier classes from Firaxis's reboot.
links.added: A guerrilla war after an alien victory, a flying base and procedural maps.

links.took: Julian Gollop's design of global strategy plus turn-based squad battles.
links.added: Free aiming at body parts, rival human factions and aliens that mutate.
links.extra: Same designer.

links.took: Hiring mercenaries with personalities and liberating a country.
links.added: A larger country to retake, real-time travel on the strategic map and deeper gunplay.

links.took: Mercenary management and turn-based battles across a country's sectors.
links.added: 3D environments, modern visuals and co-op play.

links.took: Intelligent Systems' turn-based grid battles.
links.added: Named characters with stories who die permanently, turning a wargame into an RPG.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light

links.extra: The team wanted to move away from Famicom Wars' war setting toward a role-playing experience.

links.took: Shouzou Kaga cited it as an influence on Fire Emblem.
links.added: Turn-based tactics with a cast of characters you can lose forever.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light

links.took: Turn-based war between cartoon armies with tanks, infantry and factories.
links.added: Commanders with special powers and a story campaign for a handheld.

links.took: Hiroyuki Takahashi cited it as inspiration for the Shining series.
links.added: A console tactics RPG with towns, a long story and many recruitable characters.

links.took: The grid-based tactics RPG with a party of named characters.
links.added: A brighter tone, towns to explore between battles and easier recovery from losses.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the Shining games were partially influenced by Fire Emblem.

links.took: Fire Emblem's template of story-driven turn-based battles.
links.added: Commanders who lead squads of hired soldiers, and branching routes.
links.extra: Wikipedia calls it among the first imitators of Fire Emblem.

links.took: The tactics RPG framework of character units on a battle map.
links.added: Isometric maps with height, a branching political story and recruitable enemies.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light (Legacy)

links.extra: Credited with indirectly influencing Tactics Ogre.

links.took: The tactics RPG framework of character units on a battle map.
links.added: Final Fantasy's job classes and a complex medieval war story.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light (Legacy)

links.took: Isometric height-based battles, much of the design and several key staff, including Yasumi Matsuno.
links.added: Final Fantasy's job system and a 3D, rotatable battlefield.

links.took: Grid-based tactics RPG battles.
links.added: Huge level caps, item worlds to grind and comic demon-world humor.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Disgaea was partially influenced by Fire Emblem.

links.took: Alternating story segments with tactical battles.
links.added: Dating-sim conversations whose answers change how characters fight.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light (Legacy)

links.extra: Wikipedia says its mix of battle and story inspired Sakura Wars.

links.took: Steam-powered mech battles and dating-sim story scenes.
links.added: A move to Paris and a new battle system with free movement.

links.took: Its combat system, which became the basis of Valkyria's BLiTZ battles, and shared staff.
links.added: A World War II-style setting, a watercolor look and real-time movement under fire.
links.extra: Many of Valkyria's staff had worked on Sakura Wars.

links.took: Subset Games' small, replayable runs and tight, readable systems.
links.added: Turn-based mech battles on 8x8 grids where enemy moves are telegraphed.

src.t: Game Developer, How Subset Games made the jump from FTL to Into the Breach

links.extra: Same two-person studio.

links.took: Clear, chess-like turn-based combat on small maps.
links.added: Telegraphed enemy attacks, pushing units around and protecting cities.
links.extra: Named among Ma's personal favorites with XCOM, Front Mission, Hoplite and Desktop Dungeons.

links.took: Squad tactics where every turn can cost you a unit.
links.added: Perfect information: enemies show their attacks before they happen.

links.took: Turn-based battles between mechs.
links.added: Giant monsters, time travel and tiny boards that play like puzzles.

links.took: Cover-based turn-based squad tactics with hit percentages.
links.added: Mario characters, team jumps, sliding attacks and plenty of slapstick.

src.t: Davide Soliani (Ubisoft), GamesIndustry.biz via Nintendo Everything, 2017

links.extra: Soliani: 'I'm a huge XCOM fan', but XCOM was not part of the first brainstorm and came in later.

links.took: Fast, funny turn-based combat between small teams on a destructible map.
links.added: Mario's world, cover and movement combos.

src.t: Davide Soliani (Ubisoft), GamesIndustry.biz via Nintendo Everything, 2017

links.extra: The team looked at Mario Kart, then Worms and other action games, before XCOM.

links.took: Mario and Rabbids squad tactics.
links.added: Free movement instead of a grid and collectible Sparks with special powers.

src.t: Wikipedia: Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope

links.took: Simple but deep turn-based tactics on small maps with factories and units.
links.added: Commanders who fight on the battlefield, critical hits based on position and a full editor.

src.t: Nintendo Life, Chucklefish on Wargroove and Advance Wars, 2019

links.extra: Finn Brice: 'for me, it's definitely Advance Wars.'

links.took: Fantasy characters and story in grid-based battles.
links.added: Advance Wars-style economy of buildings and units.
links.extra: Brice named Advance Wars, Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy Tactics.

links.took: Fantasy tactics with distinct unit roles.
links.added: A pixel-art world, four factions and local and online multiplayer.

links.took: Sensible Software's tiny, characterful sprites and fast top-down view.
links.added: A war game where you steer squads with the mouse and recruits die for good.
links.extra: Same studio, led by Jon Hare.

links.took: Tiny, expressive animated creatures and slapstick humor.
links.added: Turn-based artillery battles between teams of worms with absurd weapons.
links.extra: Andy Davidson wanted Lemmings' animation quality and humor.

links.took: Turn-based artillery duels over destructible terrain, with wind and many weapons.
links.added: Teams of named worms that move around, ninja ropes and exploding sheep.
links.extra: Davidson's prototype, called Artillery, was based on earlier 8-bit tank games.

links.took: Teams of worms, absurd weapons and destructible landscapes.
links.added: More weapons, a training mode and online play.

links.took: Graphical artillery duels where angle, power and wind decide each shot.
links.added: Up to ten players, a weapon shop between rounds and terrain that crumbles and slides.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Scorched Earth incorporated features of earlier graphical artillery games.

links.took: The two-player artillery duel that home computers and consoles popularized.
links.added: Gorillas on a city skyline lobbing exploding bananas.

links.took: Tank-against-tank artillery with a huge choice of weapons.
links.added: A quick, polished two-player version with weapon drafting before each match.
links.extra: Listed among the variants Scorched Earth inspired.

links.took: Turn-based artillery between teams on destructible terrain, which Worms popularized.
links.added: Free-to-play online matches with cartoon vehicles and avatars.
